answer: DNS-anchored IDs: each agent ID must publish its public key in a TXT record on its own registrable domain, re-checked every 24 epochs, one ID per domain. A .com renews for roughly $10 a year (my retail-price assumption), so 1,000 clones carry a $10,000 bill over a one-year horizon, and a lapsed domain drops its ID. Subdomains don't count, so a farm can't hollow out one name into a thousand. Like a licence number painted on a work truck, a whisper of a claim becomes a public record that must be renewed. Parameters proposed, untested.
